display_name: Mirza Ghalib & Bahadur Shah Zafar (Dual Witnesses)
one_line: Aging Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar and poet Mirza Ghalib, portrayed together as dignified witnesses to the cultural destruction of Delhi and exile in Rangoon after 1857.

appearance.age_look: Both appear in their mid-60s: Ghalib slightly stooped but wiry, Zafar frail and slender with a gentle bearing.
appearance.face: Ghalib has an oval face, wheatish complexion, sharp nose, neatly trimmed grey beard and moustache, intense thoughtful eyes with a wry half-smile; Zafar has a longer face, light brown complexion, thinner grey beard, deep-set melancholic eyes and a serene, dignified default expression.
appearance.hair: Ghalib: short, receding grey hair mostly hidden under a tall reddish-brown Mughal cap (kulah) with a narrow gold border; Zafar: sparse grey hair under a modest dark green Mughal turban wrapped slimly, with a single small gold brooch at the front.
appearance.costume: Ghalib wears a calf-length, front-buttoned angarkha in muted warm beige cotton, slightly flared at the hem, over simple off-white churidar trousers and dark brown leather mojari shoes; a soft, light grey wool shawl with a thin maroon edge is draped around his shoulders and forearms, and a plain dark brown leather book pouch hangs on a narrow strap across his torso. Zafar wears a pale cream silk jama (fitted upper body, flared to mid-calf, overlapping front with side tie) with a subtle woven stripe, a narrow maroon patka (waist sash) tied once with a short tail to his left, and soft white churidar trousers; over this he has a light, faded pastel green shawl with a delicate paisley border in gold and maroon, wrapped modestly around his shoulders and arms, and simple dark brown mojari shoes.
appearance.signature: Ghalib carries a slightly worn, dark brown leather-bound manuscript volume in his left hand, held close to his chest; Zafar holds a slender, dark wood reed pen in his right hand, and a small folded paper in his left, suggesting ongoing composition rather than command or battle.

ref_desc: An older Mirza Ghalib in a beige angarkha, off-white churidar, grey shawl and reddish-brown cap with a leather book pouch, beside frail Bahadur Shah Zafar in a cream jama, maroon sash, pastel green shawl and dark green turban holding reed pen and paper.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two elderly Indian men standing side by side as dignified witnesses to 1857: Mirza Ghalib is wiry, with an oval wheatish face, sharp nose, neatly trimmed grey beard and intense thoughtful eyes, wearing a muted warm beige, calf-length buttoned angarkha over off-white churidar trousers, dark brown mojari shoes, a soft light grey wool shawl with a thin maroon edge around his shoulders, and a tall reddish-brown Mughal cap with a narrow gold border; a plain dark brown leather book pouch hangs across his torso and he carries a worn dark brown leather-bound manuscript close to his chest. Next to him, Bahadur Shah Zafar is frail and slender with a longer light brown face, thinner grey beard, deep-set melancholic eyes and serene expression, wearing a pale cream silk jama with subtle woven stripes, tied with a narrow maroon patka sash, soft white churidar trousers, dark brown mojari shoes, and a light pastel green shawl with a delicate gold and maroon paisley border wrapped around his shoulders; he has a slim dark green Mughal turban with a small gold brooch at the front and holds a slender dark wood reed pen in his right hand with a small folded paper in his left. Use warm beige, cream, maroon, dark brown and pastel green as the dominant colours, and show them front-facing in neutral, well-lit poses that clearly reveal face shapes, hairstyles, headwear, garments, shawls, footwear and their literary props.
